name: Piramal Finance Ltd
title: Piramal Finance Ltd - 544597 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Growth RoAUM 2.0% in Q2 (up from 1.7%) with 2.5% exit-Q4 target reaffirmed; but FY28 insurance commission cap is an 18-24bp headwind and management has stopped short of FY28 guidance.

summary.headline: Piramal Finance Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 67% YoY to INR545 crores; Growth AUM up 30% YoY and RoAUM 2% annualised.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 PAT of INR545 crores (up 67% YoY) and H1 PAT above INR1,000 crores, with Growth business PBT at INR538 crores. Total AUM grew 24% YoY to INR1,13,112 crores, with Growth AUM up 30% and the legacy book down 69% YoY to INR1,673 crores. Cost to income improved to 52%, and the company raised INR3,850 crores of equity (QIP INR2,100 crores plus INR1,750 crores promoter warrants). Management reiterated FY27 profit growth guidance of around 50% and a 2.5% exit RoAUM for Q4 FY27, and flagged a possible insurance commission headwind from IRDAI's draft proposal.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail AUM INR97,462 crores, up 30% YoY; mortgages (HL plus LAP) INR64,650 crores, up 27% and 57% of AUM. Unsecured (personal, business, digital, rural micro) AUM INR23,764 crores, up 46% and 21% of AUM. Retail opex to AUM fell 5 bps QoQ to 3.48%.

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.commentary: Wholesale AUM INR13,978 crores, up 24% YoY; real estate to CMML mix 68:32, average ticket INR55 crores, yield 14.1%. Q2 disbursements INR2,615 crores against repayments of INR1,889 crores; about 74% of FY27 contractual repayments already prepaid.

segments.name: Legacy book
segments.commentary: Legacy AUM fell INR780 crores (32%) QoQ to INR1,673 crores, 1.5% of total AUM, with ECL provision of INR459 crores; separate disclosure to be discontinued after the December quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 25% (given at start of year); medium-term AUM target of about INR1.5 lakh crores by FY28 (doubling every 3 years).
FY27 profit growth guidance of about 50% YoY reiterated; management says it is confident of meeting it.
Exit Q4 FY27 Growth RoAUM target of about 2.5% reiterated, even if cost of borrowing does not fall further; management expects further opex reduction of 30-35 bps over the next 6 quarters.
Long-term RoAUM ambition above 3%; FY28 exit target now being recalibrated for the insurance commission headwind, with specific guidance to be given in Q4.
Leverage expected to rise towards 4.5x-5x in the medium term.
Overall cost of borrowing on a stock basis expected at similar or lower levels over the next 12 months despite RBI tightening.
capex_capacity: Branch network 838; no full-service urban branches added in Q2. Rural branches rose from 178 to 203.
Gold loan branches rose from 67 to 100 in Q2; target of 200 by end-March 2027.
Gold loans are a high-yield product that management is growing, partly at the expense of low-yield mortgages.
Non-dilutive regulatory capital release possible over the next 12 to 24 months; management says this plus the QIP gives runway for growth capital for some years.
Capital raise in Q2 structured to limit leverage hit; QIP added ~200 bps to CAR and 5 bps to RoAUM.
demand_pricing: Disbursements up 34% YoY in Q2, with momentum stronger than Q1.
Unsecured AUM mix at 21% (20% two quarters ago); target 25-26% over coming years. Cross-sell share of unsecured disbursements at 30%.
Mass-affluent housing loans and larger-ticket LAP showing higher growth after rating upgrade.

Incremental borrowing cost: 9.36% (H1 FY26), 8.67% (H2 FY26), 8.46% (H1 FY27). Retiring debt about 9.1% vs new borrowing about 8.4%. About INR37,500 crores of long-term borrowings mature in next 18 months (about INR29,000 crores next year per analyst).

Pricing: NBFC lending rates move with PLR; management said it will not pass on rate increases until its own cost of borrowing rises, with roughly a one-year lag and a further three-month lag to customers.
Market-linked borrowings under one-third of total; almost no repo-linked debt. Q2 raised almost nothing from capital markets, shifting mix to MCLR-linked funding.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will pass on higher rates to customers, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through follows PLR changes, which lag cost of borrowing by about one year; management expects no pass-through yet. Around 50% of assets (HL and LAP) are the main repricing book.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields rise as the legacy book runs off?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly. Q2 had one extra day, which cut retail yield by about 11 bps; management called this optical. Growth NIM should converge towards company NIM as legacy runs off.

qa_highlights.question: Is the housing loan vintage uptick real?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, driven largely by one INR4 crore fraud case from Q2 FY26; management expects it to fall in Q3. Concentration in South India IT-sector home loans persists but has not spread.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan exposure and risk strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry data shows 15-23% of gross gold disbursements went to customers 90+ days past due. Piramal's October gold disbursements to such customers are under 1%, and it will not disburse to them.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated provisioning lower than Growth credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy book write-backs (about INR90 crores profit from recovery) offset Growth credit cost, which is used to build other buffers.

qa_highlights.question: Path from 2% to 3% RoAUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex 30-35 bps further reduction over 6 quarters, funding cost reduction and mix shift to unsecured and gold; exit FY27 target 2.5%. FY28 outlook recalibrated for insurance headwind.

qa_highlights.question: How much RoAUM headwind from the insurance commission rules?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross 18-24 bps FY28 RoAUM impact if the IRDAI draft is implemented from 1 April 2027; partly offset by Pramerica Life profit share and sales-incentive rationalisation. Management says mitigating half would still be meaningful.

qa_highlights.question: Does the rising rate cycle hurt NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says rate-cycle positioning is favourable: variable-rate assets INR56,000 crores exceed variable-rate liabilities INR51,000 crores; spreads down 40-45 bps; retiring debt about 60 bps above current borrowing rates.

risks_watch: IRDAI draft on insurance commissions: 18-24 bps FY28 RoAUM gross impact if effective 1 April 2027; formal feedback to regulator planned via FIDC.
RBI tightening in H2 FY27 and rising global yields may raise borrowing costs; management expects offsets from maturing debt and rating-driven spread compression.
Gold loan industry risk: high share of customers with active gold loans (above 35%) and industry disbursements to 90+ DPD customers.
Wholesale growth headwind from high prepayments (72% of disbursements repaid in Q2).
Housing loan 90+ uptick (one fraud case) and IT-sector delinquencies in South India; management expects Q3 improvement.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profitability and funding tailwinds, with a notably cautious stance on FY28 RoAUM and the insurance commission draft, which management said it would recalibrate for once rules are final.
key_quotes: Our incremental cost of borrowing at Piramal Finance continues to decline steadily.
We don't take macro calls. We don't take decisions on everyday credit choices because of how the macro looks.
Growth is an outcome of our framework. It is not an input to our framework.
There is a INR4 crores case from Q2 of FY26, which turned out to be fraudulent, which is there in that number.
